Guangcai, also known as âWoven Gold Porcelainâ, began in the mid-to-late Kangxi period of the Qing dynasty, around the late 1600s. It took shape during the Yongzheng period and matured during the Qianlong and Jiaqing years. By the mid-Qing period, it had become a major export porcelain, alongside blue-and-white and polychrome porcelain. Pieces were sold to more than 100 countries in Europe, America and Asia.

Guangzhou was a key port for porcelain exports. Merchants brought plain white porcelain from Jingdezhen, and local painters added custom decoration to meet their customersâ requests. The craft combines traditional Chinese porcelain painting with Western painting techniques, creating a distinctive East-meets-West style. It was especially popular with European royalty and nobles, who placed special orders. Today, Guangcai remains a symbol of Guangzhouâs history as a trading port and a cherished local craft.
